    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, JSX has acquired New Pacific Airlines, and plans to bring the failed airline back with 42 seat Embraer regional jets. That’s 12 more seats than JSX sells on its planes today, and it gives them a way to grow beyond the limits of their current operation. I think this fits a company that’s been unusually creative about finding markets and figuring out how to serve them. They brought turboprops to Santa Monica’s shortened runway and used a free membership program to gain access to Teterboro in order to serve New York. JSX isn’t laying out the New Pacific strategy yet. Asked about the deal, they tell me: JSX is continually evaluating opportunities to support its long-term growth and bring its distinctive flying experience to more Customers and more communities. As part of that work, we are pursuing additional pathways that could provide even more ways to deliver our award-winning service in the future. Our focus remains on the exceptional experience, convenience, and hospitality our Customers have come to expect from JSX. New Pacific has filed its intent to resume flying and requested a waiver of the usual 45 day advance filing requirement. An operating projection calls for: Embraer ERJ145-LR aircraft with 42 seats. Two aircraft initially, growing to six by the fifth month. 10,106 flights and roughly 309,000 passenger boardings in the first year. Flights averaging about 1.2 hours gate to gate, with staffing growing to 104 employees. New Pacific used to be Northern Pacific, the startup that wanted to connect the mainland U.S. and Asia through Anchorage using Boeing 757s. It seemed unlikely to work anyway but the closure of Russian airspace to U.S. carriers kept them from even trying. It pivoted to short domestic routes and then sports and corporate charters. I reported its shutdown last November, just two weeks after it revealed an all-business class venture with beOnd. The bankruptcy process disposed of its 757s. What it has instead is Part 121 certification allowing operations beyond the 30 passenger limit of JSX’s current Part 135 public charter model. I first flew JSX home from Southwest Airlines Media Day in late 2022. JSX’s 4 p.m. departure got me home for dinner, an hour ahead of the Southwest flight I would have taken. I reached the terminal 19 minutes before departure. In Austin, I was in a Lyft less than ten minutes after touchdown. The plane was comfortable, with a seat on each side of the aisle and a side table next to mine. But getting my time back was what made it worth paying more (but honestly, not much more). I didn’t need a bigger airport lounge. I needed to spend less time at the airport. By my March 2023 visit to JSX’s headquarters, they’d fixed my one real complaint: no internet. JSX was the first carrier with Starlink, and the first to finish equipping its full fleet. Notably United Airlines owns a stake in JSX. The early JSX adoption is likely related to United’s head start with Starlink among major airlines. JSX’s business depended on putting several things together: inexpensive used aircraft, a comfortable cabin, friendly service and airports that let customers avoid wasting time. At the time, airport real estate was their biggest constraint. Finding another city with people willing to buy a ticket wasn’t enough. They needed somewhere to put the operation. Look at Santa Monica. The city is literally closing the airport and shortened its runway to 3,500 feet. JSX brought in ATR 42-600 turboprops configured with 30 seats. They found an aircraft suited to an airport that’s convenient for customers on the west side of Los Angeles, and obtained permission to operate despite the local politics. At Teterboro, the solution involved how they sold tickets. The airport prohibits publicly advertised scheduled passenger service. JSX put the flights behind a Club JSX login, limited bookings to members, and marketed the destination publicly as New York City. Joining the program is free, but joining is how they gain access to the airport. Those are different solutions to different problems. With New Pacific, JSX gains the ability to operate with more than 30 seats. My guess is that they see markets where a different version of their product could work, with more passengers sharing the cost of each departure. There is a regulatory insurance benefit. American Airlines, Southwest and the significant pilots union have pushed to restrict JSX’s business model. I anticipated that sort of campaign in my first review. Having a Part 121 operation would be useful if the rules change. But the Federal Aviation Administration’s current agenda lists its public charter rulemaking as a long-term action with the next step undetermined. They never closed the rulemaking effort. But I think it’s possible to overread the regulatory risk insurance strategy here. They could still use private terminals with a part 121 operation and 42 seats. Federal security rules provide for scheduled and public charter flights with 31 to 60 seats outside the usual secure terminal area. This wouldn’t work at every airport JSX at the moment serves due to airport certification requirements. And part 121 means different pilot requirements, including mandatory age 65 retirement (they couldn’t use their ex-American and Southwest senior captains). If they do initiative 42 seats that a different product – still more generous than a 50-seat sardine can but not nearly as spacious as the current 30-seat setup JSX appears to have a plan to add 40% more seats to some of the regional jets they own, and operate them under a scheduled airline. They haven’t remarked what they’re actually planning, but it may be a different niche than their current model rather than the assumed ‘buy a scheduled airline in case the next administration capitulates to lobbyists and puts them out of business’ the way ALPA, Southwest and American sought to do under the last administration.     #88763. Industry News: Beginner’s luck: Freshmen leave it to chance at House office lottery

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (915 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Beginner’s luck: Freshmen leave it to chance at House office lottery

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (915 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that rep.-elect Mark Teixeira reacts after drawing the worst chip during Tuesday’s lottery for newly elected members of Congress.
    • As far as birthdays go, Rep.-elect Shannon Taylor was having a pretty good one.
    • Crowded into a room in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday morning with the rest of her freshman class, the Virginia Democrat walked up to a table with a wooden box and reached in.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that rep.-elect Mark Teixeira reacts after drawing the worst chip during Tuesday’s lottery for newly elected members of Congress. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    As far as birthdays go, Rep.-elect Shannon Taylor was having a pretty good one.

    Crowded into a room in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday morning with the rest of her freshman class, the Virginia Democrat walked up to a table with a wooden box and reached in.

    “This is so nervewracking,” she remarked, before pulling out a chip with a “1” printed on it.

    It has been revealed that her prize was a coveted one — first choice of office space. Every two years, incoming members of the House play a game of chance to see who can land the best real estate and who will be relegated to less desirable corners of the Capitol complex.

    The room broke out in raucous applause and a standing ovation. Her new colleagues started singing “Happy Birthday.”.

    Not everyone was so lucky. Rep.-elect Mark Teixeira, R-Texas, pulled number 105 — the very last one. The former MLB player raised his arms in a mock celebration.

    “Lets all hope for the luck of the Taylors,” said Rep.-elect Brent Taylor, R-Tenn., only to emerge with number 81.

    The newly-elected members got their turn in a random order, walking up one by one to a table where deputy executive director of House Office Buildings Kornell Rancy kept watch over the box of chips.

    Sources indicate that rep.-elect John Cowan, R-Ga., was the first to pick a number. The first neurosurgeon to be elected to Congress, Cowan wore his white doctor’s coat as he pulled number 11 out of the box.

    “I wanted to do something where I’m just representing health care providers around the country,” Cowan stated.

    As returning members lay claim to more desirable offices made available by those who resign, retire or lose elections, the space they’ve abandoned is left for the newcomers, who are on the Hill this week for orientation. Many of them will end up in the Longworth Building, where suites can be awkward or cramped.

    Recent findings suggest that not all offices are created equal, and the calculus has changed over the years. The previously undesirable Cannon Building just underwent a budget-busting renovation that lasted more than a decade, with a spacious courtyard opening earlier this year. But the coveted Rayburn Building still retains its prestige, despite repeated and dire warnings from the Architect of the Capitol about its crumbling infrastructure.

    “You’re welcome,” remarked Rep.-elect Amish Shah, D-Ariz., after pulling a disappointing number 94.

    Prior to the lottery, Rep.-elect Trever Nehls, R-Texas, was hoping for the best but had a backup proposal in case his number stated otherwise.

    “If I don’t pick number one, I’m going to offer one of these cigars as a trade to whoever gets it,” he remarked, pointing to three of them sticking out of his jacket pocket. He’s preparing to take over the seat currently held by his twin brother Troy, who shares a fondness for stogies.

    The office space lottery dates back to 1908, when members of the 60th Congress received their first office assignments after the completion of what would be named the Cannon Building. A House page drew names and numbers from a box, and members selected their offices from a chart, according to House Office Buildings executive director of facility operations Joe Yates, who kicked things off Tuesday with a history lesson.

    The lottery now is a little more modern, with members poring over virtual office layouts and doing walkthroughs of spaces on laptops.

    “If somebody had to get 105, I’m glad it was me because I am here to serve, and I’m serving my freshman class by picking the worst office,” Teixeira remarked. “This is low on my priority list.”.

    Some members revealed their lucky draws themselves, while others let Yates break the news.

    “Come visit me,” said Rep.-elect Chris Gober, R-Texas, after pulling number 2 from the box.

    After the lottery itself, members huddled with their staff to strategize about the next steps — how to leverage their numbers and select the best suites left on the list, while also exploring layouts, paint colors and carpeting.

    Recent findings suggest that “First and foremost, a good layout, so we can do good work, and people can be comfortable in doing the work, and then a convenient location. Very utilitarian,” remarked Rep.-elect Scott Wiener, D-Calif., of his priorities.

    Industry observers note that “We’ll get a decent Longworth office,” remarked Wiener, who drew pick 43. “Cannon would have been ideal, but I’m happy with any office.”.

    Recent findings suggest that rep.-elect Manny Rutinel, D-Colo., was hoping to replicate the good luck of some of his colleagues. “I’m going to do the Shannon Taylor and Sam Forstag. It’s eyes closed, behind the back,” he said of his moves, reaching into the box. But it wasn’t enough, and Rutinel pulled number 69.

    In a recent development, “These are not red numbers, these are not blue numbers. These are the remaining numbers, and there ain’t that many,” said Rep.-elect Johnny Garcia, D-Texas, who was among the last few people to pick. He emerged with number 75.

    And when Rep.-elect Joe Strada, R-Fla., the last of the incoming members to draw, walked up to the table, the whole room cheered.

    “Wouldn’t it be crazy if I picked number 1?” he joked, pulling out the last chip in the box.

    United Nigeria Airlines Flew Passengers To The Wrong City—3 Years Later, Chairman Admits They Lied About It

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2260 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, united Nigeria Airlines flew passengers to the wrong city and blamed the weather.
    • I covered this incident on November 28, 2023, including the conflict between the pilot reportedly acknowledging a wrong flight initiative and the airline insisting on a weather diversion.
    • Executive Chairman Obiora Okonkwo revisited the episode at the World Public Relations Forum in Abuja on November 17.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, united Nigeria Airlines flew passengers to the wrong city and blamed the weather. Three years later, they’re admitting it was all a lie. I covered this incident on November 28, 2023, including the conflict between the pilot reportedly acknowledging a wrong flight strategy and the airline insisting on a weather diversion. Now, Live and Let’s Fly flags the airline chairman’s admission that the passengers’ explanation was right. Executive Chairman Obiora Okonkwo revisited the episode at the World Public Relations Forum in Abuja on November 17. A dispatcher had entered the wrong destination in the paperwork. The pilots flew there. The flight attendants apparently believed they’d reached the city everyone bought tickets to. He described the weather explanation as “just a lie” and offered this advice: “The best way of public relations is to tell the truth, but tell it responsibly.” Passengers Were Welcomed To Abuja While Sitting In Asaba On November 26, 2023, flight 0504 left Lagos with passengers booked to Abuja, Nigeria’s capital. It landed in Asaba instead, about 200 miles away. This was United Nigeria Airlines, not United Airlines. Passengers reported that the flight attendants welcomed everyone to Abuja but then everyone discovered where they actually were. November 26, 2023 — Peacock (@dawisu) Another passenger shared video: We legit got scared sha. Laff wan kee me 😅 pic.twitter.com/sWxbnJeDna— Lord Macky (@AugustineMacky) November 26, 2023 The airline’s original statement blamed “poor destination weather”, said the pilot knew about the diversion, and attributed the confusion to an incorrect cabin announcement. The plane eventually continued to Abuja. The Investigation Uncovered The Truth The flight used an Airbus A320 operated by Bulgaria’s Fly2Sky for United Nigeria Airlines. Fly2Sky said at the time that United Nigeria had assigned it a Lagos–Asaba flight the previous day and hadn’t requested a change during the pilots’ preflight briefing. The Nigerian regulator identified failures well beyond one person entering a destination incorrectly. In its findings there was: Poor coordination between United Nigeria’s operations center and the company supplying the aircraft. No joint preflight briefing between the pilots and flight attendants. United Nigeria’s failure to monitor the leased aircraft through its operations center. Failure to follow the approved flight plan filed with air traffic control. The chairman story is about a dispatch error. The regulator, though, laid out several opportunities to prevent it. British Airways Has Done It, Too In March 2019, a British Airways flight scheduled from London City to Düsseldorf went to Edinburgh after the pilots received paperwork for the wrong destination. The passengers had bought a flight to Germany but the flight took them to Scotland. A few weeks later, Scandinavian Airlines sent a Copenhagen–Florence flight to Bologna. That was a deliberate decision made before departure because the pilots lacked the correct routing information for Florence. They flew to Bologna with plans to bus passengers onward. It’s just that they kept this information to themselves. And in August 2025, I covered AirAsia X passengers being welcomed to Incheon after their Kuala Lumpur flight landed at Seoul’s Gimpo airport, about 20 miles away. Here’s the Instagram video from that coverage: View the video shared by @rizalhakimm_punyer on Instagram AirAsia X said it had intentionally diverted for fuel because bad weather had caused congestion at Incheon. It acknowledged an incorrect cabin announcement, said the captain corrected it, and offered travel vouchers. Okonkwo also used his conference appearance to discuss a passenger upset that an advertised 11:30 a.m. flight had left at 11:20. He said he’d initially wanted to shout back, but instead responded, “I apologise for United Nigeria Airline leaving on time.” An airline chairman giving a speech about accurately convey what on-time means.     Rep. James Comer releases 2027 bid for Kentucky governor

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (539 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • James Comer, here talking to reporters on Capitol Hill in June, is running for governor.
    • Comer, whose role as chairman of the House Oversight Committee gave him a powerful platform to investigate Democrats, including former Presidents Joe Biden and Bill Clinton, has launched a run for governor next year.
    • According to recent reports, the Republican, who was just elected to a sixth full term representing Kentucky’s 1st District, is seeking to succeed term-limited Democratic Gov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that kentucky Rep. James Comer, here talking to reporters on Capitol Hill in June, is running for governor. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Kentucky Rep. James R. Comer, whose role as chairman of the House Oversight Committee gave him a powerful platform to investigate Democrats, including former Presidents Joe Biden and Bill Clinton, has launched a run for governor next year.

    According to recent reports, the Republican, who was just elected to a sixth full term representing Kentucky’s 1st District, is seeking to succeed term-limited Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear. Kentucky is one of three states holding off-year gubernatorial elections in 2027, alongside Louisiana and Mississippi.

    In his announcement at a tele-town hall Monday night, Comey emphasized pocketbook complications, pledging to eliminate the state income tax and boost job-creation in Louisville.

    “If we get that income tax to zero, people are going to have more money to spend, and we're going to be able to attract more good-paying jobs to Kentucky, which will be able to keep our best and brightest in the state,’’ he said.

    As the leader of the House Oversight panel, Comer has been at the forefront in the fight over the release of records related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. (Last week, the committee released a report concluding that the federal government mishandled criminal probes into Epstein’s activities.).

    Comer is a staunch ally of President Donald Trump, who carried Kentucky by 31 points in 2024, and his hard-nosed style of politics is conveyed in a soft-spoken Southern drawl.

    It has been revealed that known back home as Jamie, Comer has deep roots in rural Monroe County, dating back to the late 1700s. Prior to coming to Congress, he operated a farm before serving 11 years in the Kentucky House. In 2011, he was elected as the commonwealth’s commissioner of agriculture.

    Sources indicate that he made an unsuccessful run for governor in 2015, losing the Republican primary by 83 votes to Matt Bevin, who went on to win the general election. The following year, Comer easily won election to the House from his western Kentucky district, succeeding Republican Ed Whitfield.

    Industry observers note that comer has moved promptly to consolidate GOP support for his gubernatorial bid. He already has the backing of Kentucky Sen. Rand Paul and Sen.-elect Andy Barr. Michael Adams, Kentucky’s term-limited secretary of state who’d been seen a potential contender, gave Comer an early endorsement this summer.

    Recent findings suggest that while Comer enters the race as the Republican front-runner, he won’t have the field to himself. Other declared hopefuls include local prosecutor Rick Hardin and distiller Charles “Bruiser” Martin, who appeared on the Discovery Channel show “Moonshiners: Master Distiller.”.

    Industry observers note that while Kentucky has in recent decades grown reliably Republican at the federal level, the GOP has won just two gubernatorial elections there over the past half century. Two high-profile Democrats have already released bids to keep the governor’s mansion in party hands: Lt. Gov. Jacqueline Coleman and former state House Majority Leader and Beshear adviser Rocky Adkins, who ran for governor in 2019.

    In a statement Tuesday, the Democratic Governors Association dismissed Comer as “a job-killing, pro-war politician who looks down on everyday Kentuckians.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An American Airlines passenger was arrested in Florida on nine charges after being denied boarding. Police say she refused to leave the Tampa airport terminal, chest bumped one officer, kicked another in the chest, and spat in a third officer’s face. Ana L. Gianaras, 34, of Grayslake, Illinois, was arrested around 3 p.m. November 8 in Airside F according to the affidavit. Guessing Headlights reported the arrest and obtained the police and court records. The booking photo comes from the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office: Police say Gianaras yelled, cursing and screaming and that her speech was slurred and her breath smelled of alcohol. She was sitting at a bar when, according to the affidavit, she got off her barstool and struck one of the officer’s chest with her own. That’s when officers say they tried to arrest her. She tensed up and tried to pull away as they struggled to handcuff her. During a search, she allegedly kicked another officer in the chest with a “reverse single leg kick.” Then, as another officer attempted to place her in the rear seat of a patrol car, police say she turned and spat in his face. Police say they found: Five cannabis cigarettes. Two plastic tubes containing suspected THC oil. 6.9 grams of orange pills identified as 30 milligram Adderall tablets. The affidavit reports preliminary positive field tests for the cannabis and oil and that she couldn’t produce a prescription for the Adderall. And once she made it to jail, sheriff’s deputies used a Taser but it’s not clear why. Her charges break down as: Six felonies: three counts of battery on a law enforcement officer, one count of resisting an officer with violence, and two counts of controlled substance possession involving the Adderall and THC oil. Three misdemeanors: disorderly intoxication, resisting an officer without violence, and possession of less than 20 grams of cannabis. She was booked at 5:21 p.m. on November 8. At her first appearance the next day, the court set bonds totaling $26,150. After two nights in jail, she was released November 10 on bond. I’ve covered an American Airlines passenger at Dallas-Fort Worth who was denied boarding for apparent intoxication and then attacked three gate agents with her phone. And there was the Orlando passenger who fled on a motorized suitcase after being refused boarding and allegedly spat at an officer. If American’s employees saw the same signs of intoxication described by police, keeping Gianaras off the plane was the right call. Their side of the story though isn’t clear. I reached out to American Airlines, and they did not respond.     Wry and Wistful Landscapes at Kansas City’s Splendid Nelson-Atkins Museum

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (283 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • ‘E verything’s Up to Date in Kansas City” — that few minutes of pure effervescence in Oklahoma refers to Kansas City circa 1907, when it was in the middle of its version of the City Beautiful movement.
    • Recent findings suggest that I visited last month and saw the very enjoyable exhibition American Prospects and Landscape Photography, 1839 to Today.
    • On “Wry and Wistful Landscapes at Kansas City’s Splendid Nelson-Atkins Museum”.

    ‘E verything’s Up to Date in Kansas City” — that few minutes of pure effervescence in Oklahoma refers to Kansas City circa 1907, when it was in the middle of its version of the City Beautiful movement. Newly introduced boulevards, new, fancy neighborhoods, hundreds of fountains, and much more were in the works. The sparkle of a new art museum was in the civic eye, too. The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art didn’t open its doors until 1933, but better late than never. It’s an essential visit for art lovers.

    Recent findings suggest that I visited last month and saw the very enjoyable exhibition American Prospects and Landscape Photography, 1839 to Today. It presents Joel Sternfeld’s lovely, often sad, wry, late-1970s and early-1980s landscape photographs in the context of the American landscape-photography genre. I love Sternfeld’s work. Born in 1944, he was the cutting-edge photographer who took color landscape photography mainstream, mostly through American Prospects, his portfolio of photographs published in book form in 1987. Color? Cutting-edge in the ’80s? Well, 1987 is about to be 40 years ago, so it qualifies as days of yore, and what has became American Prospects started in the late ’70s, when Sternfeld started an epic road trip to make art about Americans and the land. Landscape photography was, à la Ansel Adams, commonly in black and white, thought to evoke grandeur and mystery. What pushed Sternfeld to color was the advent of Kodak Vericolor III film in the 1970s. It delivered accurate, vibrant color and was good for various lighting and especially skin tones.

    Brian T. Allen is National Review’s art critic.

    On “Wry and Wistful Landscapes at Kansas City’s Splendid Nelson-Atkins Museum”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that rakuten is offering 100% back on several subscriptions, which means you can effectively buy American Express Membership Rewards points for 1 cent apiece. And if you have Bilt Silver status or higher, you can receive Bilt points at the same price. That’s the option I’d choose, because Bilt points are far more valuable. These deals can make sense even if you assign no value at all to the subscription. Spend $100 on an eligible purchase and choose 10,000 points instead of the $100 rebate. You keep the service, too. And there’s a best-ever Rakuten referral offer – Rakuten is an online shopping portal that earns points or cash back for the purchases you make anywhere, akin to the mileage malls that work with airlines like American, United, Alaska, et al. You can choose between cash back, Amex points or Bilt points. The easy, quick win before this offer is just to go to GiftCards.com through the portal and buy a $50 gift card for Uber, DoorDash, Southwest Airlines or Delta. You get $50 or equivalent points back, making this a free $50 (or better, since the points can be worth more than $50). I’ve covered using Rakuten offers to acquire inexpensive Amex points for years, and this summer’s Surfshark offer worked the same way. There are several opportunities available together now. The Current Offers Doctor of Credit flags this batch of offers. Each subscription offer is limited to a new customer or first subscription purchase, with a limit of one per Rakuten member. Merchant   Rebate   Terms That Affect The Deal Coveron, formerly NordProtect   100%   All listed individual and family subscription aims qualify. If you already earned a NordProtect rebate, the name change doesn’t make you eligible again. NordVPN   100%   Only the Basic initiative portion of Plus, Complete or Prime bundles earns rewards. Orders must go through the U.S. site. NordPass   100%   First subscription signup only. Other Nord products purchased through this offer don’t qualify. Incogni   95%   First subscription payment only, with a 40 day verification period. Surfshark   95%   First purchase only. Subscription extensions and free trial promotions don’t qualify. The 95% offers work out to 95 Amex points, or 95 Bilt points with status, per eligible dollar. That’s about 1.05 cents per point before tax. Coveron is especially interesting because Rakuten explicitly includes its full individual and family plans. At the prices Coveron advertises: Two years of individual Full Protection costs $239.76, which would generate 23,976 points at 100 points per dollar. Two years of Full Family Protection costs $647.76, which would generate 64,776 points. Those calculations assume the advertised price and 100% rate are what you see when you click through Rakuten. The family plan lets you acquire a larger block of points at the same price per point. Rakuten also states Coveron, NordVPN and NordPass are separate products, so you can qualify for each. That doesn’t override the requirement to be a new customer for the particular offer. Sales tax doesn’t earn the portal rebate. If your purchase attracts 8.25% tax, a 100 points per dollar offer costs about 1.08 cents per point. The rewards from the credit card you use to pay are on top of this though. Why I’d Take Bilt Points Over Amex Points When Rakuten added Bilt as a payout option, I preferred it to Membership Rewards. I still do, provided I’m getting the full conversion rate. For a $100 eligible purchase with a 100% rebate, here’s the choice: Payout Choice   Points Received   Cost Per Point Before Tax American Express Membership Rewards   10,000   1 cent Bilt Silver, Gold or Platinum   10,000   1 cent Bilt Blue, without elite status   5,000   2 cents You need an eligible U.S. American Express card enrolled in Membership Rewards to receive Amex points through Rakuten. Without Bilt status, I’d choose the 10,000 Amex points over 5,000 Bilt points. Bilt gives me 1:1 transfers to Hyatt, Alaska Airlines’ Atmos Rewards, United Airlines and Japan Airlines, along with partners like Air Canada Aeroplan and Air France KLM Flying Blue. Buying Bilt points for a penny gives me access to those programs without having to decide today which one I’ll use. And Bilt’s Rent Day transfer bonuses can make those points go further. Set Up The Points Payout And Keep The Paid Subscription Choose Membership Rewards in your Rakuten account settings and link your Amex account. For Bilt, link your existing Rakuten account through the Bilt app or website and select Bilt Points as the payout method. The email addresses on your Rakuten and Bilt accounts need to match. If you’re switching between Amex and Bilt, Bilt’s instructions say to select check or PayPal first, then the other points option. Start your purchase through the relevant Rakuten merchant link, check the rate, and save the offer terms and receipt. Don’t apply a coupon from somewhere else when the merchant terms exclude it. These are subscription purchases. A refund can reverse the rewards. Turning off a future renewal is different from refunding the paid term: Coveron allows you to cancel auto-renewal while keeping access through the period you’ve paid for. Rakuten pays points quarterly. The next scheduled payout is February 15, 2027, and rewards need to be confirmed to be included. A pending entry can take weeks to become payable. Bilt uses your status at payout to determine the conversion rate. And Rakuten transfers don’t count toward Bilt elite status, so this isn’t a way for a Blue member to buy their way to Silver. If you’re new to Rakuten, the referral offer adds $50 after $50 in qualifying purchases within 90 days. With an Amex payout, or Bilt’s full conversion rate, that’s another 5,000 points. On the $647.76 Coveron example, that would mean 69,776 points for $647.76 before tax—about 0.93 cents apiece.     #88754. United Airlines Is Now Worst For Checked Bags, Delta’s Cancellations Nearly Doubled—What The Latest Federal Data Demonstrates

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 34m • 📚 Deep Dive (6789 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    United Airlines Is Now Worst For Checked Bags, Delta’s Cancellations Nearly Doubled—What The Latest Federal Data Demonstrates

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 34 min read (6789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~34 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • United Airlines is now worse than American at handling checked bags.
    • Sources indicate that the latest federal airline statistics show some results that don’t fit the usual reputations.
    • Recent findings suggest that the Department of Transportation’s November Air Travel Consumer Report covers September and the first nine months of 2026.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    United Airlines is now worse than American at handling checked bags. Delta’s cancellation rate has nearly doubled. And American, which has spent years bumping more passengers than any other airline, cut involuntary denied boardings 84% in the third quarter. The latest federal airline statistics show some results that don’t fit the usual reputations. It also shows why calling an airline “premium” requires more than nicer seats and better wifi. Strong operational performance isn’t enough but it’s the table stakes. An airline needs to get the basics right first, including delivering bags alongside their owners, as close to on-time as possible. The Department of Transportation’s November Air Travel Consumer Report covers September and the first nine months of 2026. Here’s the domestic flight performance through September, and I take a look at how this performance compares to earlier trends. Airline   On time2025   On time2026   Canceled2025   Canceled2026 Alaska Airlines*   77.44%   78.64%   1.01%   1.30% Delta Air Lines   79.57%   78.31%   1.19%   2.25% United Airlines   76.77%   76.20%   1.34%   1.75% American Airlines   73.09%   73.30%   2.57%   2.99% Southwest Airlines   78.10%   73.08%   0.85%   0.96% Allegiant Air   74.69%   72.59%   0.44%   0.73% Frontier Airlines   69.96%   70.21%   1.78%   2.15% JetBlue Airways   73.42%   67.74%   1.43%   4.08% Every airline listed canceled a larger share of flights than a year earlier. American ranks fourth for punctuality with an improvement of just 0.21 percentage points. Southwest and JetBlue each lost more than five points. United’s Premium Pitch Gets Ahead Of Its Operation United has improved its cabins, technology and network. I’ve argued that its broader schedule explains a lot of the customer preference Scott Kirby attributes to the brand. It’s a better airline than it used to be. Its operational results still don’t support treating it as anything close to an all-around leader. United blames the locations of its hubs, and says that it does well considering where it opreates. Its annual report points to hubs at the “most congested and constrained airports in the country.” It also benchmarks departures against competitors at its own hubs, rather than treating all airports as equally easy places to operate. In September, the category covering air traffic control, airport operations, traffic volume and ordinary weather accounted for delays on 8.57% of United’s flights, versus 5.78% at Delta. United also canceled a smaller percentage of flights than Delta or American through September, and it ranks third for on-time arrivals. But its punctuality declined and its cancellation rate rose from 1.34% to 1.75%. That’s nearly a 1/3 increase. And the weaknesses extend beyond on-time performance and completion factor. United ranks last for mishandled baggage. American was worst in full-year 2024, while United finished last in 2025. United remains last for the first nine months of 2026, and finished last separately in July, August and September. Here are mishandled bags per 1,000 checked bags, with a lower number being better. This includes delayed, damaged, lost and stolen bags. Airline network   Jan.–Sept. 2025   Jan.–Sept. 2026 Allegiant Air   0.9   1.3 Southwest Airlines   3.9   3.2 JetBlue Airways   3.1   3.4 Delta Air Lines   4.2   3.6 Alaska Airlines*   5.1   5.0 Frontier Airlines   3.8   5.2 American Airlines   6.8   6.6 United Airlines   7.4   6.9 United mishandles bags at nearly twice Delta’s rate. American remains last if you look only at the mainline airline: 7.2 per 1,000, versus United’s 6.6. United Express drags down United’s network result, while American Eagle improves American’s. Missed connections can cause bags to miss flights, too. So baggage problems aren’t entirely independent of congested hubs and delayed aircraft. Passengers buying connecting travel, though, have choices on which airline to connect and United doesn’t get a pass there because its hubs are less reliable. Then there are wheelchairs. United and Delta handled almost identical volumes: 105,534 at United and 105,559 at Delta. United mishandled 1,269. Delta mishandled 373. Delta Warned That Its Problems Would Last Through Summer. They Did. Back in May, I covered Delta’s cancellation problems and its executives’ warning that fixing them would take through the summer. Pilot availability, crew scheduling and recovery after disruptions were central problems. Chief Operating Officer Dan Janki said, “It’ll take us a little bit of time here as we work through it through the summer.” And Delta’s pilots didn’t actually go along with changes to contractual provisions that would boost reliability. They want something in return, and Delta hasn’t been willing to pay. Delta’s cancellation rate rose about 89%, from 1.19% to 2.25%. Subtracting the first-half figures from the latest report gives a third-quarter cancellation rate of 2.08%, versus 1.13% a year earlier. This is still a problem. Southwest’s Boarding Changes Had Costs That Were Easy To See Coming I warned before Southwest introduced checked bag fees that pushing luggage into the cabin would slow boarding and create more gate checking. Assigned seating then removed the incentive to board quickly to grab the best available seat, while making passengers hunt for bin space near a particular row. By March, flight attendants were pushing back over the consequences. Southwest was trying to get more flying out of its aircraft while making boarding less efficient. Through September, Southwest’s on-time arrival rate fell from 78.10% to 73.08%. Southwest handled 71.1 million checked bags, down from 84.7 million, while scheduling almost exactly the same number of domestic flights. That’s 16% fewer checked bag enplanements, now that they charge most passengers separately. People are now carrying their bags into the cabin instead of checking them as often. JetBlue’s Nice Onboard Product Can’t Make Up For Their Operation I’ve long described JetBlue as good in the air and a mess on the ground. Mint can be excellent. Even coach offers has been relatively pleasant, although JetBlue is enshittifying it in order to make room for domestic first class seating. But the operation lets down the product. The first nine months were bad: 67.74% on time and 4.08% canceled, both worst in the industry and their cancellation rate was nearly three times the same period last year. The summer was worse. Combining the July, August and September figures, only 61.85% of scheduled flights arrived on time during the third quarter. JetBlue canceled 6.28%, about one in sixteen flights. In July alone, it canceled nearly one in ten. September improved substantially, to 71.98% on time and 2.13% canceled. JetBlue still finished last on both measures that month. Actually getting a handle on this won’t fix JetBlue’s finances. They’re a baseline for a turnaround. Disruptions add expense, make repeat business harder to win, and undermine the value of the product the airline is spending money to improve. JetBlue needs customers to be able to buy its flight without budgeting for everything going wrong. Alaska Has Been A Perennial Leader Alaska leads the network on-time rankings at 78.64% and canceled 1.30% of its flights. That’s a better cancellation rate than any of the three largest network airlines. This is a longstanding strength. Back in 2015, I was asking why Alaska didn’t get more recognition for running such a strong operation when Delta received so much of the credit. Buying Hawaiian added an operation benefiting from the islands’ generally favorable weather. I pointed out that statistical advantage last year, and Hawaiian is now included in Alaska’s figures. But Alaska’s ability to run a good airline wasn’t something it bought with Honolulu. It was doing that long before the acquisition. American’s Bumping Numbers Are Finally Changing American involuntarily bumped 684 passengers in the third quarter, down from 4,318. That’s an 84% reduction, with almost unchanged passenger volume. Mainline American’s count fell nearly 90%, from 2,042 to 208. I broke the news of American’s newly introduced mandate against involuntary bumping. Airport managers can approve more compensation to find volunteers. Employees are supposed to keep the door open and take a delay if necessary. Volunteers can even be confirmed onto the very next departure when it’s already full. That directive took effect September 30. Nearly the entire quarter measured here came before it. The 84% decline shows the improvement that was already underway as American became more willing to pay volunteers. There’s another American improvement buried in the network totals. Comparing the third quarter with the same period last year: Mainline cancellation rate: improved from 2.21% to 1.46%. Regional partner cancellation rate: worsened from 2.44% to 3.17%. Combined network: almost unchanged, from 2.33% to 2.34%. American’s own flights became materially less likely to cancel over the summer, while American Eagle erased that improvement in the combined result. The bumping change also leaves Frontier looking particularly bad. It accounted for 69% of all involuntary bumps in the third-quarter table, despite carrying about 4% of the passengers. Delta secured 49,231 volunteers that quarter and involuntarily bumped nobody. Frontier recorded 841 volunteers and 2,514 involuntary bumps or roughly three unwilling passengers for every volunteer.     Sources indicate that the latest federal airline statistics show some results that don’t fit the usual reputations. It also demonstrates why calling an airline “premium” requires more than nicer seats and better wifi. Strong operational performance isn’t enough but it’s the table stakes. An airline needs to get the basics right first, including delivering bags alongside their owners, as close to on-time as possible.

    Recent findings suggest that the Department of Transportation’s November Air Travel Consumer Report covers September and the first nine months of 2026. Here’s the domestic flight performance through September, and I take a look at how this performance compares to earlier trends.

    Every airline listed canceled a larger share of flights than a year earlier. American ranks fourth for punctuality with an improvement of just 0.21 percentage points. Southwest and JetBlue each lost more than five points.

    It has been revealed that united has improved its cabins, technology and network. I’ve argued that its broader schedule explains a lot of the customer preference Scott Kirby attributes to the brand. It’s a better airline than it used to be. Its operational results still don’t support treating it as anything close to an all-around leader. United blames the locations of its hubs, and states that it does well considering where it opreates. Its annual report points to hubs at the “most congested and constrained airports in the country.” It also benchmarks departures against competitors at its own hubs, rather than treating all airports as equally easy places to operate. In September, the category covering air traffic control, airport operations, traffic volume and ordinary weather accounted for delays on 8.57% of United’s flights, versus 5.78% at Delta. United also canceled a smaller percentage of flights than Delta or American through September, and it ranks third for on-time arrivals. But its punctuality declined and its cancellation rate rose from 1.34% to 1.75%. That’s nearly a 1/3 increase. And the weaknesses extend beyond on-time performance and completion factor. United ranks last for mishandled baggage. American was worst in full-year 2024, while United finished last in 2025. United remains last for the first nine months of 2026, and finished last separately in July, August and September. Here are mishandled bags per 1,000 checked bags, with a lower number being better. This includes delayed, damaged, lost and stolen bags. Airline network   Jan.–Sept. 2025   Jan.–Sept. 2026 Allegiant Air   0.9   1.3 Southwest Airlines   3.9   3.2 JetBlue Airways   3.1   3.4 Delta Air Lines   4.2   3.6 Alaska Airlines*   5.1   5.0 Frontier Airlines   3.8   5.2 American Airlines   6.8   6.6 United Airlines   7.4   6.9 United mishandles bags at nearly twice Delta’s rate. American remains last if you look only at the mainline airline: 7.2 per 1,000, versus United’s 6.6. United Express drags down United’s network result, while American Eagle improves American’s. Missed connections can cause bags to miss flights, too. So baggage problems aren’t entirely independent of congested hubs and delayed aircraft. Passengers buying connecting travel, though, have choices on which airline to connect and United doesn’t get a pass there because its hubs are less reliable. Then there are wheelchairs. United and Delta handled almost identical volumes: 105,534 at United and 105,559 at Delta. United mishandled 1,269. Delta mishandled 373. Delta Warned That Its Problems Would Last Through Summer. They Did. Back in May, I covered Delta’s cancellation problems and its executives’ warning that fixing them would take through the summer. Pilot availability, crew scheduling and recovery after disruptions were central problems. Chief Operating Officer Dan Janki stated, “It’ll take us a little bit of time here as we work through it through the summer.” And Delta’s pilots didn’t actually go along with changes to contractual provisions that would boost reliability. They want something in return, and Delta hasn’t been willing to pay. Delta’s cancellation rate rose about 89%, from 1.19% to 2.25%. Subtracting the first-half figures from the latest report gives a third-quarter cancellation rate of 2.08%, versus 1.13% a year earlier. This is still a problem. Southwest’s Boarding Changes Had Costs That Were Easy To See Coming I warned before Southwest introduced checked bag fees that pushing luggage into the cabin would slow boarding and create more gate checking. Assigned seating then removed the incentive to board swiftly to grab the best available seat, while making passengers hunt for bin space near a particular row. By March, flight attendants were pushing back over the consequences. Southwest was trying to get more flying out of its aircraft while making boarding less efficient. Through September, Southwest’s on-time arrival rate fell from 78.10% to 73.08%. Southwest handled 71.1 million checked bags, down from 84.7 million, while scheduling almost exactly the same number of domestic flights. That’s 16% fewer checked bag enplanements, now that they charge most passengers separately. People are now carrying their bags into the cabin instead of checking them as often. JetBlue’s Nice Onboard Product Can’t Make Up For Their Operation I’ve long described JetBlue as good in the air and a mess on the ground. Mint can be excellent. Even coach offers has been relatively pleasant, although JetBlue is enshittifying it in order to make room for domestic first class seating. But the operation lets down the product. The first nine months were bad: 67.74% on time and 4.08% canceled, both worst in the industry and their cancellation rate was nearly three times the same period last year. The summer was worse. Combining the July, August and September figures, only 61.85% of scheduled flights arrived on time during the third quarter. JetBlue canceled 6.28%, about one in sixteen flights. In July alone, it canceled nearly one in ten. September improved substantially, to 71.98% on time and 2.13% canceled. JetBlue still finished last on both measures that month. Actually getting a handle on this won’t fix JetBlue’s finances. They’re a baseline for a turnaround. Disruptions add expense, make repeat business harder to win, and undermine the value of the product the airline is spending money to improve. JetBlue needs customers to be able to buy its flight without budgeting for everything going wrong. Alaska Has Been A Perennial Leader Alaska leads the network on-time rankings at 78.64% and canceled 1.30% of its flights. That’s a better cancellation rate than any of the three largest network airlines. This is a longstanding strength. Back in 2015, I was asking why Alaska didn’t get more recognition for running such a strong operation when Delta received so much of the credit. Buying Hawaiian added an operation benefiting from the islands’ generally favorable weather. I pointed out that statistical advantage last year, and Hawaiian is now included in Alaska’s figures. But Alaska’s ability to run a good airline wasn’t something it bought with Honolulu. It was doing that long before the acquisition.     Delta secured 49,231 volunteers that quarter and involuntarily bumped nobody. Frontier recorded 841 volunteers and 2,514 involuntary bumps or roughly three unwilling passengers for every volunteer.

    #88752. What Republicans don’t know about Black voters’ resilience cost them

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1006 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    What Republicans don’t know about Black voters’ resilience cost them

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1006 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sen.-elect Scott Colom speaks during a victory rally at Tougaloo College on Nov.
    • The campaign of Mississippi’s Sen.-elect Scott Colom was rightfully praised for its clever and brutal ads.
    • Industry observers note that however, it was fitting that the Democrat’s closing message traded the edge for a solemn reminder of who and what brought him so far on his journey to his election as Mississippi’s first Black U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sen.-elect Scott Colom speaks during a victory rally at Tougaloo College on Nov. 11. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images).

    The campaign of Mississippi’s Sen.-elect Scott Colom was rightfully praised for its clever and brutal ads. The “pick another protein” spot will forever be stuck in the brains of a huge swath of Americans, especially Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. She underestimated Colom and his team, and will soon be an ex-senator.

    Industry observers note that however, it was fitting that the Democrat’s closing message traded the edge for a solemn reminder of who and what brought him so far on his journey to his election as Mississippi’s first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction.

    The ad delivered an all-American lesson about history, born of bravery and sacrifice.

    Filmed at the Jackson, Miss., home of slain civil rights leader Medgar Evers, the ad featured Colom recounting the story of Evers, a World War II veteran who survived Normandy, only to be shot in the back by a racist assassin, resentful that a Black man dared to exercise his rights as a citizen in the country he fought for.

    “He was killed for helping Mississippians vote,” Colom stated. “On Tuesday, use your vote and honor everyone who died for that right.”.

    In a state where voting is still racially polarized, it was clear that Colom would not win over a majority of white voters; he won an estimated 25 percent, better than Democrats in recent elections and cutting into Trump’s margins, but certainly not a path to victory.

    Black voters in Mississippi made the difference, as they often have. With their allies in the cause of justice, they heeded the call. They showed up despite the state’s stringent and often confusing voting restrictions, purges of the voting rolls engineered by Republican Secretary of State Michael Watson (who used unverified data from a credit bureau), and the U.S. Supreme Court Louisiana v. Callais decision that led to a wave of Southern states breaking up Black-majority districts.

    When the Mississippi purges resulted in “affidavit ballots” that required verification to count, as The Washington Post reported, young Black women tracked down those voters, one by one, to do everything they could to ensure voters’ efforts were not in vain.

    Black voters mattered in states all over the country, but especially in the South, where low turnout has plagued Democrats, particularly in midterm elections.

    In a recent development, keisha Lance Bottoms was elected the first Black female governor in the country in Georgia, where Democrats won up and down the ballot. Newly elected senators Annie Andrews in South Carolina and James Talarico of Texas campaigned for and earned support from Black voters with proposals that rose above platitudes. And don’t sleep on North Carolina, where voters flipped seats the GOP tried to gerrymander into a hardened majority. The sight of hundreds of students from HBCU NC A&T State University, denied a campus early voting site, marching to the polls, must have made the ancestors smile.

    In Florida and Louisiana, where Democrats had little financial support and lost their statewide races, Black voters brought them tantalizingly close to victory and energized for the contests to come.

    I still don’t expect Republicans to give up the election shenanigans, done in the name of “election integrity” and color blindness but in reality designed to demoralize as much as suppress. Why try to win over a diverse electorate with an inclusive, policy-driven message when manipulating Black-majority districts can still work?

    Sources indicate that the number of Black U.S. House members in the next session of Congress will fall, offset by a few Democrats who survived in redrawn districts, including Shomari Figures of Alabama and Don Davis of North Carolina.

    But you can’t redistrict a state, and you can’t skip town halls and expect tradition, support for the Confederacy and an “R” after your name to forever save you — the Hyde-Smith playbook.

    Recent findings suggest that "I blocked Scott Colom from being a federal judge, and you blocked him from being U.S. senator," she bragged, too soon, on election night.

    Maybe she should have emphasized affordability, saving rural hospitals and serving all Mississippians, as Colom did.

    What did GOP officials in those Southern red states think they would accomplish by focusing on their base and ignoring everyone else in states they were supposed to be serving?

    Did they not pay attention in history class, or maybe they attended one of those post-integration private schools where an unedited version of America’s past might not have been on the lesson plan?

    Did they believe that voters who remembered Evers, Fannie Lou Hamer, Vernon Dahmer and countless others would shrug and say “you win” when legislatures and elections officials quickly and cynically pounced to quiet their voices?

    That would be disrespectful to all the people who worked for, sometimes died for rights they knew they may never enjoy, yet had a belief in America and the rightness of their cause.

    Scott Colom and the Evers family remembered. He was emotional in his reaction, in an MS NOW interview, when asked about the statement from Reena Evers-Everette, daughter of Medgar and Myrlie Evers. “Their courage helped make this moment possible,” she remarked.

    Industry observers note that colum agreed: “I absolutely stand on their shoulders. And from the bottom of my heart, I’m going to do everything I can to make them proud.”.

    Post-election, he has been very gracious, saying that he intends to serve all Mississippians, including the woman whom I suspect would hit a different note if the election had turned in her favor.

    I have no doubt Scott Colom means it. He knows who paid the price to get him this far.

    It has been revealed that mary C. She is host of the CQ Roll Call “Equal Time with Mary C. Curtis” podcast. Follow her on X @mcurtisnc3.

    Attorney General Todd Blanche, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, White House chief of staff Stephen Miller and other administration officials have moved to military installations or protected government housing.

    Under Bessent, Treasury introduced Operation Economic Outcast in August to disrupt Iran’s oil-smuggling, financial and cryptocurrency networks.

    BESSENT WARNS IRAN'S OUTSIDE BACKERS TO 'STAY AWAY' AS TRUMP SEEKS TO 'ASPHYXIATE' TEHRAN'S ECONOMY.

    Since then, Treasury has targeted Iran’s oil-smuggling shadow fleet, sanctioned eight Canada-based money services businesses it claims helped Iranian entities move funds and moved to cut crypto exchange MEXC Global off from the U.S. financial system over alleged illicit transactions.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The next frontier for the Airbus A321XLR is South America.
    • After opening dozens of new transatlantic routes, the long-range narrow-body will make its debut with LATAM Airlines in March 2027.
    • LATAM, a close partner of Delta Air Lines, will outfit its fleet of XLRs with 174 seats.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The next frontier for the Airbus A321XLR is South America.

    After opening dozens of new transatlantic routes, the long-range narrow-body will make its debut with LATAM Airlines in March 2027. The airline has yet to say which routes the XLRs will fly, but executives have previously outlined opportunities to connect the U.S. and South America.

    LATAM, a close partner of Delta Air Lines, will outfit its fleet of XLRs with 174 seats. Business class will feature 12 lie-flat suites supplied by Thompson Aero Seating in a 1-1 layout with privacy doors.

    The suites include 19-inch personal entertainment screens, Bluetooth connectivity and in-seat charging options.

    In a recent development, economy features 13-inch screens at each of the 126 seats, which are supplied by Recaro, plus Bluetooth connectivity and USB-C outlets. The cabin includes 36 extra-legroom seats.

    “The Airbus A321XLR allows us to take our value proposition to the next level and elevate the travel experience for our passengers,” noted Paulo Miranda, the chief customer officer of LATAM, in a statement. He described the interior, which features red, orange and blue hues, as “inspired by South America.”.

    According to recent reports, LATAM executives have noted it could fly the XLR on routes into the U.S. from its hub at Jorge Chavez International Airport (LIM) in Lima. However, those prepares were called into question in May over the addition of a "connection fee" at LIM.

    The airline and Delta serve six U.S. destinations from LIM: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL), Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), Miami International Airport (MIA), John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK), Orlando International Airport (MCO) and, since January 2026, Salt Lake City International Airport (SLC).

    LATAM did not comment on specific route aims for the XLR.

    It has been revealed that the XLR is the second new airplane type for LATAM in as many years. The airline took delivery of its first Embraer E195-E2 in October. It will use the small jet to expand its feeder network in Brazil and support additional long-haul, intercontinental flying.

    The business behind it is restaurant financing: inKind buys future food and beverage credit, then sells or awards it to diners. Restaurants get money now and customers later.

The $5.03 difference is small enough that different credit card earnings could change which purchase is better. The amount you pay for inKind Cash doesn’t expire. The promotional portion has a three year expiration. Neither purchase earns another round of inKind rewards when you spend the prepaid balance. New members can still get $25 off a first qualifying $50 meal through my referral link. I receive referral credit when you qualify.     #88747. Latest Update: Some records in Ilhan Omar case will be released, judge states

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (468 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Some records in Ilhan Omar case will be released, judge states

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (468 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., speaks during a news conference at the Capitol last summer.
    • It has been revealed that A judge noted he will order the release of some information about the federal investigation into Rep.
    • District Court for the District of Columbia made the statement Tuesday during a hearing brought by news organizations and an advocacy group seeking details about the search.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., speaks during a news conference at the Capitol last summer. Few details have emerged so far about the government’s search of her home earlier this fall. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    It has been revealed that A judge noted he will order the release of some information about the federal investigation into Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., which included a search of her Washington house last month.

    Judge James Boasberg for the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia made the statement Tuesday during a hearing brought by news organizations and an advocacy group seeking details about the search. Boasberg ordered the government to provide him by Friday what could be disclosed in the case. He pointed to how investigators are handling the “speech or debate” clause immunity that Omar has as a sitting member of Congress.

    “This is purely legal questions, interesting questions, about the privilege, the extent of the privilege and how it would apply,” Boasberg stated.

    The Constitution includes an immunity for members of Congress for the “speech or debate” they engage in as part of their jobs.

    Sources indicate that boasberg also directed the government to propose redactions to the as-yet secret docket. While he mentioned next week’s expected disclosures would not include the 67-page document that investigators provided to justify the search, he left the door open to unsealing that down the road if the government closes the case or brings charges.

    Justice Department attorney Alessandra Serano argued against broad disclosures, calling it “very rare that a precharging, pre-indictment unsealing would happen.”.

    The high-profile nature of the investigation leaked into the courtroom Tuesday, as Boasberg cited statements by President Donald Trump and others about the investigation into Omar.

    “You have had administration officials, prominent ones, talking about the purpose of the investigation,” Boasberg stated.

    Administration officials have accused Omar of committing immigration crimes for years, and Trump said last month the DOJ was looking into Omar “strongly.” Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on a recent podcast that investigators had served multiple search warrants and were investigating possible immigration fraud tied to when Omar entered the United States as a child.

    Separately, Boasberg remarked he may glitch rulings in the coming weeks unsealing portions of other court cases tied to the investigation, including one brought by Omar herself earlier this month seeking the return of the items seized in the search.

    The administration executed the search warrant in October, just a few weeks before the midterm elections. The timing of the search drew accusations of political bias from Democrats who claimed that the administration brought the case to sway the midterm elections.

    For years Trump has mentioned he wanted criminal charges to be brought against his political foes, including Omar and others in Congress.

    Industry News: The Homeland Security Secretary Is Now A Hologram—Praising President Trump While You’re Stuck In Line At Airport Security

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1276 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is appearing as a hologram at airport security checkpoints.
    • In a recent development, the government already makes you stand in line and submit to a search before you can board your flight.
    • Will Stancil photographed the display at Minneapolis–St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is appearing as a hologram at airport security checkpoints. At Minneapolis–St. Paul, a traveler indicates the recording reassures passengers they aren’t the problem, obsequiously thanks President Trump, and closes with “God Bless America.” The government already makes you stand in line and submit to a search before you can board your flight. This adds a modern 1984 element to the experience. Will Stancil photographed the display at Minneapolis–St. Paul, describing Mullin as a “lunkhead Big Brother.” Mullin’s upper body floats inside a diamond-shaped display mounted on a pedestal, presiding over the security line. So there’s now a hologram of Markwayne Mullin addressing the security line at the MSP airport, telling travelers that while security is important, he’s sure we’re not the problem, and thank you President Trump, and God Bless America, like some kind of lunkhead Big Brother — Will Stancil, November 20, 2026 A Chicago Tribune photograph taken November 13 documents a Mullin hologram playing on a loop at O’Hare. And the reaction isn’t confined to Bluesky. A traveler on Reddit’s O’Hare forum described seeing Mullin’s hologram while stranded after the nationwide ground stop. The post’s title: “Apparently we can afford holograms of cabinet secretaries at airports, just not a functioning air traffic control system.” Back on October 14, a Charlottesville traveler complained about a Mullin checkpoint video crediting President Trump with a golden age of travel. Writing in the health technology publication HIStalk on November 16, Dr. Jayne described longer than usual security lines and chuckling at a Mullin video promising that “Golden Age of travel.” Every minute someone spends waiting in a TSA line, the less popular you become. I’m not sure this is as good an ego boost as DHS secretaries seem to think it will be. Campaign3D says it deployed 50 Tensator Shard displays across 27 U.S. airports. The justification for sticking the image of Big Brother in front of the masses was to make security instructions more noticeable. Here’s the supplier’s photograph of the display telling passengers to keep electronics in their bags: The system uses HYPERVSN technology. Its floating image comes from rapidly rotating LED elements, so “hologram” is the marketing description. It’s just putting a politician on a very elaborate fan. And while knowing whether your laptop stays in your bag in a given lane could be useful, praise for the president doesn’t help speed through the checkpoint. I’ve written about the way checkpoint advertising monetizes a compulsory audience. TSA creates the audience, and private companies sell access to it through advertising on the bins passengers have to use. Here the administration is using the same compulsory setting to sell itself. It’s like A Clockwork Orange, the novel turned into a Stanley Kubrick film, where Alex has his eyelids clamped open while being forced to watch violent footage, including Nazi imagery, after being given drugs that make him nauseated. You don’t have to stare at Mullin. You do have to remain in the screening process if you want to take your flight. It’s an campaign ad you can turn off. Mullin’s predecessor did this, too. Kristi Noem appeared on checkpoint screens blaming Democrats for the October 2025 government shutdown. Dallas–Fort Worth and Dallas Love Field declined to show the video, citing their policies against political advertising. When Noem later tried to suspend PreCheck and Global Entry, I wrote that she had become “literally the face of long screening lines at airports.” Mullin seems determined to give that phrase another dimension. Back in July, Mullin’s office emailed asking whether any Noem videos were still playing at airports or other ports of entry. It instructed airports to “please kindly remove them as soon as possible and provide confirmation of removal.” He wanted to erase memories of his predecessor (“we’ve always been at war with Eurasia”) to make room for his own visage. (HT: Paul H.)     #88745. Southwest Prepares To End The Wait For Extending Its Schedules—11 Month Rolling Calendar Is Coming, Report Notes

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4180 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Southwest Prepares To End The Wait For Extending Its Schedules—11 Month Rolling Calendar Is Coming, Report Notes

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4180 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that southwest Airlines looks to stop making customers wait for batches of fresh flight dates and move to a rolling booking calendar roughly 11 months into the future, more like other airlines operate, according to a new report by Enilria.
    • I checked Southwest’s own booking calendar.
    • Sources indicate that there’s some history here that helps explain what’s changing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that southwest Airlines looks to stop making customers wait for batches of fresh flight dates and move to a rolling booking calendar roughly 11 months into the future, more like other airlines operate, according to a new report by Enilria. That would make it easier to lock in a family vacation or flights to a cruise—and give its international partners more opportunities to sell trips that include Southwest connections. I checked Southwest’s own booking calendar. They’re accepting reservations through September 29, 2027. Their next extension is planned for December 17, when they’ll open flights through November 6, 2027. That’s 324 days into the future. That December release is still a batch. The blueprint to replace these releases with a rolling window isn’t something I’ve seen anywhere other than from Enilria. Southwest Has Already Sold Flights More Than 300 Days Ahead There’s some history here that helps explain what’s changing. On April 26, 2024, Southwest unveiled its first booking window exceeding 300 days. It was selling travel through March 5, 2025—313 days ahead. At the time, Southwest said its historical range had been 180 to 250 days, citing vacation planning, meetings and groups, Hawaii, and its international destinations as reasons to sell further out. With batch releases, though, the window shrinks every day until the next extension. You might be able to book ten months ahead on release day, then considerably less several weeks later. A rolling calendar keeps adding dates. The reported change would give customers roughly the same planning horizon whenever they shop, without needing to track Southwest’s next release announcement. Shorter Schedules Meant Fewer Reservations To Fix I wrote about Southwest’s tradeoff back in 2020: waiting to publish let the airline offer a firmer schedule, but cost them customers who wanted to commit earlier. An airline can decide where to put its planes before selling the seats, or sell a provisional schedule and fix customers’ reservations when its plans change. Southwest preferred to finish more of that work first. That gave them room to adjust for seasonal demand and aircraft availability without disrupting as many purchased trips. Their technology made changing flights expensive. In a 2010 investor presentation, then-CEO Gary Kelly explained that when Southwest canceled a flight: we have to manually rebook every single customer on that flight Southwest completed its move to Amadeus Altéa in May 2017. This allowed for automated rebooking during disruptions, better connection planning, and more sophisticated inventory management. So the technology that makes a longer selling window practical has been there for years. The commercial case for using it has grown. International Partners Have A Reason To Want More Dates Southwest increasingly needs to appear wherever customers are shopping. I explained how the Expedia deal would change their incentives when it was announced in 2025. If a customer searches dates Southwest isn’t selling, competitors get the business before Southwest even enters the comparison. The airline had already expanded booking capabilities through agency reservation systems in 2020. More recently, SAP Concur shut down its old Southwest direct connection in July 2025 as Southwest’s new fare structure required a different booking path. And Southwest now lists 12 international airline partners, including Icelandair, EVA Air, Singapore Airlines, Turkish Airlines, and newly added French bee. These combined itineraries are sold through the partners’ websites and distribution channels. A foreign airline can have its flight available for sale while Southwest hasn’t opened the domestic connection yet. The partner can’t problem the complete itinerary using that Southwest flight. It may sell a connection on another U.S. airline instead and Southwest loses the passenger. That makes partner sales a strong reason to extend the window. The underlying partnership work also predates Elliott Management’s intervention. I covered Southwest recruiting to build airline partnerships in June 2022. And the longer schedule announcement came in April 2024. Even a roughly 330 day window won’t match every overseas partner. EVA Air sells flights up to 360 days ahead. This would narrow the gap, while still leaving some early international bookings out of Southwest’s reach. Earlier Booking Comes With More Time For Plans To Change Selling earlier gives Southwest more chances to win customers. Direct bookings bring cash in sooner. The recurring benefit comes from business Southwest otherwise would’ve lost, or from selling its existing seats more profitably. Against that are distribution costs, servicing reservations, and the work of repairing itineraries when schedules change. Customers should expect more exposure to schedule revisions when booking further ahead. A departure can move, a nonstop can become a connection, and a changed domestic flight can break the connection to an international departure. With assigned seating, moving passengers also means dealing with their seat selections. And the first day a flight goes on sale isn’t necessarily its cheapest day. Opening dates and opening inexpensive inventory are separate decisions. In fact, airlines may hold back cheap fares waiting to see how flights sell, and also figuring that eager buyers may be less price-sensitive. And there’s a real a problem buying Southwest’s cheapest cash tickets this far ahead. As I’ve covered before, Basic fare credits expire six months after the original purchase. Southwest notes a voluntary cancellation after that deadline produces no flight credit. If you buy a Basic ticket 11 months ahead, then cancel two months before departure, you’ve already passed that deadline by three months. The original reservation is valid, but you get nothing if you cancel. I’d be much more comfortable using Rapid Rewards points for a speculative booking that far out. Cancel at least 10 minutes before the original departure and the points go back to the account, without the six month expiration attached to the cash fare.
